summary: Initial discovery for Cypress Health evaluating Redwood for embeddings + reranking. Customer wants hybrid search with vector DB integration, throughput targets ~200 QPS at P99 latency < 200ms for top-K retrieval, and a reranker step for improved precision. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private trade-offs, dimensionality choices (768 vs 1536), and benchmarking plan.
transcript:
00:00 - Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on your account, with me is Jordan our solutions engineer and Samir from CSM.
00:08 - Alex Moreno: Hey all, Alex here, CTO at Cypress Health. Thanks, we'll be brief.
00:12 - Priya Singh: Hi, Priya. Head of ML. We mostly want to understand how Redwood fits into our retrieval + rerank pipeline.
00:20 - Jordan Liu: Awesome, thanks. High-level, are you currently using any vector DB today or pure ES/OpenSearch?
00:25 - Leah Kim: We're prototyping with Pinecone and a small FAISS cluster for local tests.
00:30 - Daniel Park: And the plan is to replace some of our keyword search + boosting with embeddings to handle semantic queries.
00:36 - Maya Patel: Great, that aligns with a lot of customers. Quick qual questions: target QPS, latency SLOs, and whether data residency or VPC is a requirement?
00:45 - Priya Singh: Target is approx 100-200 QPS steady, peaks at ~350. P95 under 120ms ideally, P99 under 200ms for the retrieval step. Reranker can be warmer and allowed higher latency, maybe up to 400-500ms.
01:00 - Jordan Liu: Ok that's helpful. For that profile, we usually recommend embeddings in 1536 dims for best precision on our models, but 768 is cheaper and often fine depending on docs. What are typical doc sizes?
01:12 - Leah Kim: Most docs are short clinical notes and biodata, around 200-400 tokens per doc. We do have some long transcripts, but we chunk them.
01:22 - Alex Moreno: Security is a must: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration \u0004 we have to keep PHI in our VPC for the pilot.
01:30 - Maya Patel: Understood. We have Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem, with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM options. Our hosted API can be used with strict data retention policies too but for PHI we typically see customers prefer Dedicated or Private.
01:43 - Priya Singh: Can you explain the typical architecture for retrieval + rerank on Redwood?
01:48 - Jordan Liu: Sure. A common pattern: bi-encoder embeddings for fast nearest-neighbor retrieval (hosted in your vector DB like Pinecone/Milvus/Weaviate or our managed store), retrieve top-K (e.g., 100), then lightweight cross-encoder reranker or a small transformer on Redwood Dedicated to re-score top results. That gives best precision.
02:04 - Daniel Park: How about hybrid search \u0004 BM25 plus embeddings? We currently do BM25 boost for exact matches.
02:09 - Jordan Liu: Hybrid is common. You can combine BM25 scores with cosine distances. We recommend normalizing scores and applying a tunable weight; Redwood Console allows you to observe score distributions and suggest weights. There's some fuzz in the transcription: our consoles sometimes shows 'kay vee cache' when it's actually KV cache.
02:24 - Priya Singh: What about vector dimensionality and storage cost? 1536 dims will increase index size. Any tooling to recommend dims?
02:30 - Jordan Liu: Yes, Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and dimensionality based on your workload. For clinical short docs, 1536 often yields better recall; however if cost is a constraint 768 with re-ranking still performs well. We also support quantized embeddings and lower precision to reduce storage.
02:45 - Alex Moreno: Throughput: can Redwood handle 200 QPS for retrieval + rerank? We're worried about per-token costs for the reranker.
02:52 - Jordan Liu: For pure retrieval via vector DB it's mostly the DB throughput. For reranking, if you run a cross-encoder on Dedicated GPUs, we can handle hundreds of queries per second with batching. We have options: Dedicated reserved pools for steady throughput, or Hosted with burst capacity. For cost-sensitive pipelines, you can do bi-encoder + smaller reranker or even a learned lightweight scorer.
03:14 - Maya Patel: Another option is to offload most of the compute to the vector DB for retrieval and do reranking only for the top 10-20 results to reduce cost. That often hits the sweet spot.
03:24 - Priya Singh: Do you support direct connectors to Milvus/Weaviate or do we have to push to your managed store?
03:29 - Jordan Liu: We have connector docs and customers commonly use Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, or even OpenSearch with dense vector fields. For Dedicated/Private, connectors run inside your network. For hosted we can ingest and manage; for private we can integrate with your VPC and KMS.
03:44 - Daniel Park: What about latency guarantees? We need SLA language for Dedicated.
03:48 - Maya Patel: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, and enterprise contracts include SLOs for tail latency for our inference endpoints. We'll share the SLA doc.
03:55 - Alex Moreno: Encryption at rest and audit logs are non-negotiable.
03:58 - Maya Patel: We support KMS integrations and detailed audit logs in Redwood Console. Private deployments can integrate with HSMs for key custody.
04:07 - Priya Singh: For reranking models - are you suggesting Redwood-hosted models or can we bring our own?
04:12 - Jordan Liu: Both. You can bring your own fine-tuned reranker (we support standard model formats) and run on Dedicated or Private. For hosted we provide verified model profiles. We also have quantization and kernel selection to optimize performance.
04:25 - Leah Kim: Any gotchas with batching and KV cache? We heard Redwood has a KV caching mechanism for auto-complete and prefix caching.
04:32 - Jordan Liu: Yes, KV cache reduces repeated prefix computation for decoder models, but for rerankers which are encoder-only it's less relevant. For generation-heavy paths Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and smart routing to keep latency predictable.
04:46 - Priya Singh: Can we do a small POC - 10k documents, 2k benchmark queries, and measure recall/precision and latency?
04:51 - Maya Patel: Absolutely. Typical POC flow: share dataset, we run baseline with your current vector DB + our hosted embeddings, run a rerank experiment on Dedicated, then compare metrics. We'll also surface cost estimates.
05:02 - Alex Moreno: Sounds good. Timeline - we'd like a pilot in the next 3 weeks.
05:06 - Maya Patel: We'll aim to deliver a POC plan within two days; Jordan can follow up with a technical checklist.
05:11 - Priya Singh: One more Q - how do you handle model versioning and rollouts? We want to test multiple embedding models and roll back if quality drops.
05:18 - Jordan Liu: Redwood supports model versioning and rollouts in the Console; you can pin models per route and do canary tests with automatic fallback. We also integrate evals so you can tie regressions to specific prompt sets.
05:32 - Daniel Park: For the reranker, what's the expected cost per 1k queries? Even rough numbers help.
05:36 - Maya Patel: We'll include rough per-1k numbers in the pricing sheet; depends on model size and whether it's batched on Dedicated. For example, a small cross-encoder on Dedicated might be $X per 1k, while hosted larger models could be 3-5x that. We'll give concrete numbers.
05:50 - Priya Singh: Any notable competitors we should consider?
05:53 - Maya Patel: Many teams look at Pinecone or Weaviate for vector DBs, and some use cloud-native options like OpenSearch. For managed reranking, some use OpenAI or third-party inference providers. We'll share differentiators.
06:05 - Alex Moreno: Ok, recap and next steps?
06:08 - Maya Patel: Recap: POC with 10k docs, 2k queries, target 100-200 QPS, prioritize 1536 dims but try 768 for cost comparisons, run hybrid BM25+emb pipeline and a top-K rerank. Action items: pricing sheet, technical deep dive, dataset share. We'll get the POC plan out by 2027-03-24.
06:28 - Priya Singh: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
06:30 - Maya Patel: Thanks, bye.
